steps.title: Distance is not the cause
steps.say: Actually, Earth is closest to the Sun in January during northern winter! The 23.5-degree axial tilt, not the distance, causes the seasons.

ops.text: Distance vs. Tilt: Earth is closest in January!

steps.title: Summer solstice tilt
steps.say: Here in June, the Northern Hemisphere tilts directly toward the Sun, concentrating sunlight and making days longer.

steps.title: Opposite hemispheres
steps.say: Notice that while the north enjoys summer, the southern hemisphere tilts away into winter, which wouldn't happen if distance were the cause.

steps.title: Explore the orbit
steps.say: Drag Earth along its orbit to see how the tilt changes the angle of sunlight throughout the year.
